However, the effectiveness of such agreements often hinges on the willingness of countries to uphold their commitments. Disparities in economic capabilities and historical responsibilities for emissions complicate negotiations and implementation. Wealthier nations are often called upon to provide financial and technological support to developing countries, enabling them to pursue sustainable development pathways.

Social equity is also a crucial element of climate change policy. Vulnerable communities—often the most affected by climate impacts—frequently lack the resources to adapt or recover. Policymakers must ensure that climate strategies incorporate measures to protect these populations, fostering resilience and inclusivity. This can include investments in green infrastructure, access to clean energy, and support for local adaptation initiatives.

In conclusion, effective climate change policy must navigate a complex landscape of economic, social, and political factors. questions.solution:
The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a successor to VAT used in India on the supply of goods and service. Both VAT and GST have the same taxation slabs. It is a comprehensive, multistage, destination-based tax: comprehensive because it has subsumed almost all the indirect taxes except a few state taxes.

The GST Council was established as a constitutional body under Article 279A of the Indian Constitution.

The tax came into effect from 1 July 2017 through the implementation of the One Hundred and First Amendment to the Constitution of India by the Government of India. 1 July is celebrated as GST Day. The GST replaced existing multiple taxes levied by the central and state governments.

Goods and services are divided into 5 different tax slabs for collection of tax: 0%, 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%. However, petroleum products, alcoholic beverages, and electricity are not taxed under GST and instead are taxed separately by the individual state governments, as per the previous tax system.

India Currently Recognize four types of goods service tax returns. These are: CGST, SGST, IGST and UTGST.

questions.question: The Treaty of Srirangapatnam was signed in 1792 between Tipu Sultan of Mysore and who among the following representatives of the British East India Company?
questions.questionHtml: The Treaty of Srirangapatnam was signed in 1792 between Tipu Sultan of Mysore and who among the following representatives of the British East India Company?
questions.solution:
The Treaty of Seringapatam signed 18 March 1792, ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War. Its signatories included Lord Cornwallis on behalf of the British East India Company, representatives of the Nizam of Hyderabad and the Maratha Empire, and Tipu Sultan, the ruler of Mysore.

Under the treaty, Tipu Sultan had to cede half of his kingdom's territory to the British and their allies—the Marathas and the Nizam of Hyderabad. He also had to pay a substantial war indemnity of 33 million rupees. Additionally, two of Tipu Sultan's sons were taken hostage by the British as a guarantee for the payment. The territory ceded included the Malabar Coast, Mangalore, Coimbatore, and the Dindigul district.

This treaty significantly weakened Mysore's power and marked a strategic victory for the British, further consolidating their control over southern India. It also showcased the British strategy of forming alliances with local rulers to expand their influence in the Indian subcontinent.
